mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized) signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of quarters with GDPC1 growth above 2.5% (annualized) over the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.0% indicates monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) reflects a tight labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS up and UNRATE down) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%) triggers aggressive monetary policy, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity attractiveness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Above-average industrial production (INDPRO > 105) indicates strong manufacturing activity, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 105, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1,300,000 units (HOUST > 1300) signal robust consumer demand and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1300, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong nominal retail sales (RSAFS) combined with low inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates rising real consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS up and CPIAUCSL down) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), the Federal Reserve's policy actions increase borrowing costs and reduce economic growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
